concepts.title: Machine Learning Model Accuracy
concepts.definition: Machine learning is the branch of AI where a computer tunes its own model from examples rather than following hand-written rules. The model is first fitted on training data and then judged on separate testing data; its accuracy is the share of test cases it gets right, expressed as a percentage.
concepts.key_idea: Train on one batch, judge on another; accuracy is simply right answers divided by total test answers times 100.
question_patterns: a trained model answered 186 of 200 test cases correctly; find its accuracy percentage
how is a machine learning model trained and tested before deployment
calculate the accuracy of a spam filter that classified 45 emails correctly out of 50
what distinguishes machine learning from traditional programming
a prediction model scored 92 percent accuracy on 100 test cases; how many were correct
state the role of training data in building a machine learning model

solution_steps.action: form the fraction of correct answers
solution_steps.explain: divide the number of correct predictions by the number of test cases

solution_steps.action: convert the fraction to a percentage
solution_steps.explain: multiply the ratio by 100 to report accuracy as a percentage

worked_examples.q: A model gets 72 of 80 test cases right. What is its accuracy in percent?

concepts.title: Big Data Characteristics: the Five V
concepts.definition: Data sets too large or messy for ordinary DBMS tools are called big data. Five traits set such data apart: sheer size (Volume), the speed at which it arrives (Velocity), the mix of structured and unstructured forms (Variety), how trustworthy the readings are (Veracity), and the useful knowledge hidden inside that justifies processing cost (Value).
concepts.formula: big_data_traits = volume + velocity + variety + veracity + value
concepts.key_idea: Remember the five V labels and what each guards against: size, speed, mixture, reliability, and worth.
question_patterns: list the five characteristics of big data and explain each in one line
which characteristic of big data refers to the trustworthiness of the data
name the characteristic of big data that describes the rate of generation of data
structured, semi-structured and unstructured data together show which V of big data
why is value considered a characteristic of big data
write a short note on big data and its characteristics

solution_steps.action: match each V to its meaning
solution_steps.explain: volume = size, velocity = arrival rate, variety = mixed forms, veracity = trustworthiness, value = useful insight

solution_steps.action: attach a real example to each trait
solution_steps.explain: tweets arriving every second show velocity; their mixed text, images and links show variety

solution_steps.action: state why ordinary tools fail
solution_steps.explain: traditional DBMS software cannot cope with data this large, fast and unstructured

worked_examples.q: Which V of big data names the sheer size of the data?

concepts.title: Big Data Volume Growth Arithmetic
concepts.definition: Web traffic, smartphone posts and sensor feeds together create data on a colossal scale, roughly 2.5 quintillion bytes every day. Converting such a flow into hourly or yearly totals is straightforward division and multiplication on the byte count.
concepts.key_idea: A per-day rate turns into any other period by dividing or multiplying by the number of hours or days in that period.
question_patterns: about 2.5 quintillion bytes of data are created each day; estimate the yearly total in bytes
find how many bytes of data are generated per hour given a daily creation rate
a sensor network produces 12 terabytes daily; compute its output for a 30-day month
why is the pace of data generation increasing according to the chapter
a video platform uploads 900 hours of footage per day; how many hours in a non-leap year
express one quintillion as a power of ten and as numerals

solution_steps.action: reduce the daily rate to an hourly rate
solution_steps.explain: split the day's bytes evenly across 24 hours

solution_steps.action: scale the daily rate up to a year
solution_steps.explain: multiply the daily bytes by the number of days in a non-leap year

worked_examples.q: A sensor feed creates 3 gigabytes per hour. How many gigabytes does it create in 24 hours?

concepts.title: Cloud Service Models IaaS PaaS SaaS
concepts.definition: Cloud providers deliver three standard service levels: IaaS rents raw computing hardware such as virtual machines and storage, PaaS hands developers a ready-made build-and-run platform with the needed software pre-installed, and SaaS gives end users on-demand access to finished applications on subscription.
concepts.key_idea: The lower the model in the stack, the more the user configures; the higher, the more is managed by the provider.
question_patterns: differentiate between IaaS, PaaS and SaaS with one example of each
a company wants virtual server provisioning and on-demand storage to deploy custom applications; which cloud model fits
which cloud service model would you choose to edit documents online and why
a developer wants a pre-configured Apache server with MySQL and Python ready; name the suitable model
name the government of India cloud initiative and its purpose
how does pay-per-use charging work in cloud computing

solution_steps.action: place each model on the stack
solution_steps.explain: IaaS supplies machines, PaaS supplies a ready platform on those machines, SaaS supplies finished applications

solution_steps.action: ask what the user still manages
solution_steps.explain: IaaS users configure the setup, PaaS users control only their deployed application, SaaS users just use the software

solution_steps.action: attach a everyday example
solution_steps.explain: rented virtual machines = IaaS; a pre-built Python web host = PaaS; online office suites = SaaS

worked_examples.q: Which cloud model rents raw virtual machines and storage?

concepts.title: Pay Per Use Cloud Billing
concepts.definition: Cloud resources are charged like electricity: the customer pays only for what was consumed. A typical bill adds a usage charge for computing time to a separate charge for stored data, each computed at its own rate.
concepts.key_idea: Bill each consumed resource at its own rate, then add the parts; no upfront investment is needed.
question_patterns: a startup ran 40 compute hours at 8 per hour and stored 250 GB at 2 per GB; find the cloud bill
justify that storage of data is cost effective in cloud computing for a small business
compute the monthly charge for 30 hours of virtual machine usage at 10 per hour plus 100 GB storage at 3 per GB
why is on-demand service economical for a five-friend startup with a limited budget
a user doubles both compute hours and storage; what happens to the bill if rates stay fixed
compare upfront server purchase cost with pay-per-use charging for a short project

solution_steps.action: price the computing time used
solution_steps.explain: multiply the hours of usage by the per-hour rate

solution_steps.action: price the stored data
solution_steps.explain: multiply the gigabytes kept in cloud storage by the per-GB rate

solution_steps.action: add the two charges
solution_steps.explain: the payable bill is the sum of both usage charges

worked_examples.q: A cloud bill charges Rs 4 per compute-hour for 100 hours plus Rs 2 per GB for 50 GB stored. What is the total in rupees?

concepts.title: Grid Computing Parallel Task Split
concepts.definition: A grid joins geographically scattered computers, called nodes, into a kind of virtual supercomputer. A large job is divided into subtasks that run in parallel on the nodes at the same time, so the waiting time shrinks roughly in proportion to how many nodes share the work.
concepts.key_idea: Splitting one job across n parallel nodes makes each node do a fraction of the units, cutting total waiting time.
question_patterns: a job of 9000 units is split evenly over 6 grid nodes, each unit taking 2 minutes; how long does the run take
differentiate between cloud computing and grid computing with suitable examples
what are nodes in a grid and what role do they play
state the difference between a data grid and a processor grid
why is middleware needed to set up a grid
compute the per-node load when 12000 subtask units are shared by 8 nodes

solution_steps.action: divide the job across the nodes
solution_steps.explain: integer-divide the total units by the number of grid nodes to get each node's share

solution_steps.action: convert a node's share into time
solution_steps.explain: multiply the per-node units by the minutes each unit takes; nodes run in parallel so this is the whole job's time

worked_examples.q: A grid of 5 nodes splits 200 equal units evenly. How many units does each node process?

concepts.title: Blockchain Append Only Ledger
concepts.definition: A blockchain keeps a shared ledger on every participating computer instead of one central database. Valid transactions are sealed into blocks, each block carries a header visible to all nodes while private data stays with its owner, and a new block joins the chain only after every node authenticates it, which makes the record practically impossible to alter secretly.
concepts.key_idea: Every node holds the full chain, so a change must fool all copies at once; entries are added but never silently edited.
question_patterns: explain how blockchain technology keeps a transaction ledger secure
what is a block header in a blockchain and who can see it
why can no single member of a blockchain network alter stored data
prepare two situations, such as scholarship distribution, where blockchain promotes transparency
how does a decentralised database differ from a centralised one used by banks
what must happen before a new block is added to the chain

solution_steps.action: check who holds the record
solution_steps.explain: each participating node keeps a full copy of the ledger rather than one central owner

solution_steps.action: check how an entry is accepted
solution_steps.explain: all nodes must authenticate the transaction before its block joins the chain

solution_steps.action: test a tampering attempt
solution_steps.explain: a single altered copy disagrees with every other copy, so the tamper is exposed

worked_examples.q: In a blockchain of 20 nodes, how many copies of the ledger exist?

concepts.title: Internet of Things and Web of Things
concepts.definition: The Internet of Things links everyday objects fitted with embedded hardware and software so they can exchange data over a network, letting users control appliances remotely. The Web of Things goes one step further by using standard web services as the single interface, avoiding the need for one separate app per device. Sensors such as the accelerometer and gyroscope in a phone feed these systems with real-world input.
concepts.key_idea: IoT connects objects to each other; WoT reuses the web itself as the one interface for all of them.
question_patterns: what do you understand by the Internet of Things? list two potential applications
how are IoT and WoT related
why would controlling n devices otherwise need n different apps
name the two phone sensors that detect orientation and rotation
how can IoT concepts turn a school into a smart school? give two examples
match each situation to the smart application it illustrates: medication reminder, parking alert

solution_steps.action: check what is being connected
solution_steps.explain: IoT connects physical objects with embedded controllers; a plain computer network connects computers

solution_steps.action: check which interface is used
solution_steps.explain: IoT apps talk per device, while WoT reuses standard web services so one interface reaches every thing

solution_steps.action: identify the sensing layer
solution_steps.explain: smart sensors pick up physical inputs, like an accelerometer reading the phone's tilt, and pass processed data on

worked_examples.q: Which extension of IoT reuses standard web services as the single interface for all devices?
